text.p: Following are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAWN

- Caretaker Interior Minister Umar Afridi said the government is holding talks with the Mohajir National Movement (MQM) for releasing people who were arrested during the tenure of the former government on charges of terrorism.

- Chief Justice Sajjad Ali Shah has constituted a seven-member bench to hear the petition filed by ousted prime minister Benazir Bhutto challenging the dissolution of the National Assembly and dismissal of her government.
- Two unidentified gunmen shot dead a leader of the Shi'ite militant Sipah-i-Muhammad and seriously injured his nephew in the town of Chichawatni in the Punjab province.

- The caretaker government will pay 700 million rupees to International Business Machines (IBM) as compensation for losses sustained after the caretaker government cancelled a 3.0 billion rupee contract for computerisation of national identity cards.
- The Chief Election Commissioner will announce on December 16 the schedule for holding general elections on February 3.
- The second Clinton administration will pay more attention to South Asia as the U.S. has immense security and economic interests in the region, Assistant U.S. Secretary of State Robin Raphel said.
BUSINESS RECORDER
- The government has decided to modify the private sector power policy by replacing the pre-fixed buy-back tariff with competitive rates to be decided through bidding, sources said.
- The gap between Pakistan's exports and imports in July-November was about $1.510 billion, 13.46 percent down from the same period last year when it was $1.745 billion.
- The state's Corporate Law Authority has allowed the launching of Pakistan's second credit rating agency in which Duff & Phelps Credit Rating will have a 40 percent stake.
- The Pakistan Mint has stopped minting coins of all denominations in absence of further orders from the State (central) Bank of Pakistan owing to a sharp decline in use of the metal currency.
FINANCIAL POST

- HSBC Investment Bank of Britian has served the state-run Oil and Gas Development Corporation with a legal notice for unilateral cancellation of its appointment as financial adviser for disinvestment of 49 percent of OGDC's shares.

- Pakistan is holding talks with Japanese securities firms for possible issue of Samurai bonds but sources said the launching of a yen-denominated bond by Pakistan was not imminent pending work on documentation which could take several weeks.
THE NATION
- The United States has voiced hopes that Pakistan and India will soon resume serious high-level talks which will also cover the core issue of Kashmir without preconditions.
- The Balochistan government is facing a financial crisis and has stopped all payments except salaries of its employees.
-- Islamabad newsroom 9251-274757
